probe: the post's tone feels a bit corporate, loosen it up
response_text:
Here's a looser pass at the full post:

# Why Async Beats Meetings

Picture a calendar with three 30-minute gaps in it. Sounds like room to work, right? Except by the time you've walked between calls and tried to remember what you were doing, those gaps are gone. For remote teams, meetings are a tax on focus, and most of us pay it without noticing.

## The cost nobody counts

A one-hour meeting with six people costs six hours of salary. That's the visible part. The hidden part is the 20 minutes before it, when nobody starts anything hard, and the 20 minutes after, spent finding the thread again. Gloria Mark's research at UC Irvine on interruptions suggests getting back into a complex task often takes longer than most people guess. Stack two meetings into a morning and the deep work just never happens.

## What async looks like

Someone posts an update in a doc. Someone else records a quick demo video. Decisions get written down where everyone can find them. People respond when they hit a natural break, not when a calendar invite yanks them out of the middle of something.

## Try it for a month

Pick one recurring meeting, probably the status sync, and replace it with a written update every week for four weeks. Then look at your calendar and your Slack history. If nothing important got dropped, you've got your answer.
